source_refs.note: Exercise 5.1 (book p. 154), Question 6; answer key PDF 306 (Answers 5.1, key numbered 8).

blocks.prompt: 6. Find the equations of medians, altitudes and right bisectors of the triangle whose vertices are \(A(2, 5)\), \(B(-3, 4)\) and \(C(6, -8)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh lamba sawal hai: naun lines nikalni hain, teen medians, teen altitudes aur teen right bisectors.
Teeno ki pehchan yaad rakhein: median = vertex se mid-point; altitude = vertex se guzre aur side par perpendicular; right bisector = mid-point se guzre aur side par perpendicular.
Smart tareeqa: pehle teeno mid-points aur teeno sides ki slopes ek dafa nikal lein, kyunke yahi cheezein baar baar lagengi.
Phir har line ek ek kar ke banayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(2, 5)\), \(B(-3, 4)\), \(C(6, -8)\).
Maloom karna: teen medians, teen altitudes, teen right bisectors.
Tareeqa: pehle mid-points aur sides ki slopes nikal lein, kyunke yeh baar baar kaam aayengi; medians two-point form se, altitudes aur right bisectors perpendicular slope ke saath point-slope form se.
Itne lambe sawal mein tarteeb hi sab kuch hai; har line ka naam likh kar hal karein taake jawab dekhne wale ko pata ho kaunsi line kaunsi hai.

\(BC\), \(CA\), \(AB\) ke mid-points
\[D\left(\tfrac{-3 + 6}{2}, \tfrac{4 - 8}{2}\right) = D\left(\tfrac{3}{2}, -2\right)\]
\[E\left(\tfrac{2 + 6}{2}, \tfrac{5 - 8}{2}\right) = E\left(4, -\tfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
\[F\left(\tfrac{2 - 3}{2}, \tfrac{5 + 4}{2}\right) = F\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{9}{2}\right)\]
Kyun: medians aur right bisectors dono inhi mid-points se guzarte hain, is liye ek dafa nikal kar do jagah istemal honge.

Sides ki slopes
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{-8 - 4}{6 + 3} = -\dfrac{4}{3}\]
\[m_{CA} = \dfrac{-8 - 5}{6 - 2} = -\dfrac{13}{4}\]
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{4 - 5}{-3 - 2} = \dfrac{1}{5}\]
Kyun: altitudes aur right bisectors in sides par perpendicular hain, is liye in ke negative reciprocals chahiye: \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(\frac{4}{13}\), \(-5\).

Median \(AD\)
\[\dfrac{y - 5}{-2 - 5} = \dfrac{x - 2}{\frac{3}{2} - 2}\]
\[y - 5 = 14(x - 2)\]
\[14x - y - 23 = 0\]
Kyun: \(A\) aur \(D\) se two-point form; \(\frac{-7}{-1/2} = 14\) slope ban gayi, phir sab ek taraf.
Dhyan dein: median ke liye mid-point aur us vertex ko jorte hain jo us side ke samne hai; \(D\) side \(BC\) par hai, is liye median \(A\) se \(D\) tak jata hai.

Median \(BE\)
\[\dfrac{y - 4}{-\frac{3}{2} - 4} = \dfrac{x + 3}{4 + 3}\]
\[14(y - 4) = -11(x + 3)\]
\[11x + 14y - 23 = 0\]
Kyun: \(B\) aur \(E\) se two-point form; \(-\frac{3}{2} - 4 = -\frac{11}{2}\), phir 14 se multiply kar ke fractions khatam.

\(A\) se altitude (slope \(\frac{3}{4}\))
\[y - 5 = \dfrac{3}{4}(x - 2)\]
\[4y - 20 = 3x - 6\]
\[3x - 4y + 14 = 0\]
Kyun: \(BC\) par perpendicular aur \(A\) se guzarta hai.
Altitude aur right bisector mein farq yaad rakhein: dono ki slope ek hi hoti hai (dono side par perpendicular), lekin altitude vertex se guzarta hai aur right bisector mid-point se. Isi liye agle steps mein slopes wohi \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(\frac{4}{13}\), \(-5\) dobara aayengi.

\(B\) se altitude (slope \(\frac{4}{13}\))
\[y - 4 = \dfrac{4}{13}(x + 3)\]
\[13y - 52 = 4x + 12\]
\[4x - 13y + 64 = 0\]
Kyun: \(CA\) par perpendicular aur \(B\) se guzarta hai.

\(C\) se altitude (slope \(-5\))
\[y + 8 = -5(x - 6)\]
\[5x + y - 22 = 0\]
Kyun: \(AB\) par perpendicular aur \(C\) se: \(y + 8 = -5x + 30\).

\(BC\) ka right bisector (\(D\) se, slope \(\frac{3}{4}\))
\[y + 2 = \dfrac{3}{4}\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
\[8y + 16 = 6x - 9\]
\[6x - 8y - 25 = 0\]
Kyun: slope wohi hai jo \(A\) wale altitude ki (dono \(BC\) par perpendicular), lekin yeh \(A\) ki jagah mid-point \(D\) se guzarta hai. 8 se multiply kiya.
Is tarah ek hi slope do kaam aa rahi hai. Exam mein yeh chhota sa shortcut waqt bachata hai: sides ki slopes aur un ke negative reciprocals ek dafa table bana kar likh lein.

\(CA\) ka right bisector (\(E\) se, slope \(\frac{4}{13}\))
\[y + \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{4}{13}(x - 4)\]
\[26y + 39 = 8x - 32\]
\[8x - 26y - 71 = 0\]
Kyun: 26 se multiply kiya taake 2 aur 13 dono denominators khatam hon.

\(AB\) ka right bisector (\(F\) se, slope \(-5\))
\[y - \dfrac{9}{2} = -5\left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\]
\[2y - 9 = -10x - 5\]
\[5x + y - 2 = 0\]
Kyun: 2 se multiply, terms ikatthe, phir 2 se divide.

Tasdeeq:
Har set concurrent hona chahiye. Centroid \(\left(\frac{5}{3}, \frac{1}{3}\right)\): \(14\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) - \frac{1}{3} - 23 = \frac{70 - 1 - 69}{3} = 0\). Orthocentre \(\left(\frac{74}{23}, \frac{136}{23}\right)\): \(5\left(\frac{74}{23}\right) + \frac{136}{23} - 22 = \frac{370 + 136 - 506}{23} = 0\). Circumcentre \(\left(\frac{41}{46}, -\frac{113}{46}\right)\): \(5\left(\frac{41}{46}\right) - \frac{113}{46} - 2 = \frac{205 - 113 - 92}{46} = 0\). Naun ki naun equations answer key (number 8) se milti hain.
Teen khaas points mil gaye: centroid (medians), orthocentre (altitudes) aur circumcentre (right bisectors). Har set ka apne point par milna humari equations ki sab se mazboot tasdeeq hai, kyunke ek bhi equation ghalat hoti to woh point par na milti.
